title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{1.4} Let $(R,\frak{m})$ be a local complete ring of dimension $d$. Let  $\frak{a}$ be an ideal of dimension one. Then
 $$\begin{array}{ll} \  \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R)=0, \   when \ \  d >2,
\end{array}$$
in particular $\operatorname{Coass}_R \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R)= \emptyset$.
 $$\begin{array}{ll} \ \operatorname{Coass}_R \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R) \subseteq \{ \frak{m} \}, \   when\ \  d =1,
\end{array}$$
and in the case $d=2$ we have
 $$\begin{array}{ll} \ \operatorname{Coass}_R \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R)= \bigcup^r_{i=1} \operatorname{Coass}_R(\widehat{R_{\frak{p}_i}}) =  \{ \frak{p}_1,..., \frak{p}_r \}  \cup  (\bigcup^s_{j=1} \{\frak{q}_j : R_{\frak{p}_i}/\frak{q}_j R_{\frak{p}_i} \text{ is not complete } \}) ,
\end{array}$$
where $\frak{p}_1 ,... \frak{p}_r$  are minimal prime ideals of  $\frak{a}$ and  $\frak{q}_1 ,... \frak{q}_s$  are minimal prime ideals of  $R$ with $\frak{q}_j \subseteq \frak{p}_i$ for $i \in \{1,...,r \}$.

In particular $\operatorname{Cosupp} \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R)$ is closed for all $d >0$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{2.1} Let $\frak{a}$ be an ideal of  a  local ring $(R,\frak{m})$ and $M$ a finitely generated $R$-module of dimension $d$. Then $ \mathfrak{F}^d_{\frak{a}}(M)$ is Artinian. Furthermore
$$\begin{array}{ll} \operatorname{Att}_R (\mathfrak{F}^d_{\frak{a}}(M)) =  \{\frak{p} \in \operatorname{Ass} M: \dim R/\frak{p} =d \} \cap V(\frak{a}).
\end{array}
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Independence Theorem we may assume that $\operatorname{Ann} M=0$ and so $d=\dim R$. As $H^d_{\frak{m}} (M/\frak{a}^n M)$ is right exact ($n \in \mathbb {N}$), we have
$$\begin{array}{ll} H^d_{\frak{m}} (M/\frak{a}^n M) & \cong H^d_{\frak{m}} (R) \otimes_R M/\frak{a}^n M
\\& \cong H^d_{\frak{m}} (M) \otimes_R R/\frak{a}^n
\\& \cong H^d_{\frak{m}} (M)/\frak{a}^n H^d_{\frak{m}} (M).
\end{array}$$
Since $H^d_{\frak{m}} (M)$ is an Artinian module so there exists an integer $n_0$ such that for all integer  $t \geq n_0$ we have  $\frak{a}^t H^d_{\frak{m}} (M) = \frak{a}^{n_0} H^d_{\frak{m}} (M)$. Then one can see that
$$\begin{array}{ll} \mathfrak{F}^d_{\frak{a}}(M) \cong  H^d_{\frak{m}} (M)/\frak{a}^{n_0} H^d_{\frak{m}} (M),
\end{array}$$
which is an Artinian module. By virtue of above equations and  \cite  [ Theorem 7.3.2]{Br-Sh}, the second claim is clear.
$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box
head: manual

title: Lemma
body_md: \label{2.2} Let $(R,\frak{m})$ be a complete local ring and $M$ a finitely generated $R$-module. Then $\operatorname{Supp} (\mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M))=\bigcup_{\frak{p} \in \operatorname{Ass}_R \mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M)} V(\frak{p})$. Moreover $\operatorname{Supp} (\mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M)) \cap V(\frak{a}) \subseteq V(\frak{m})$ .
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
To prove the claim, it is enough to consider that $\operatorname{Ass}_R \mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M)=\{ \frak{p} \in \operatorname{Ass}_R M: \dim R/(\frak{a} +\frak{p})=0 \}$ (cf. \cite  [ lemma 4.1]{Sch}) .
$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box
head: manual

title: Proof
body_md:
$(1)\Rightarrow (3)$ and  $(2)\Rightarrow (1)$ are obvious.


 $(3)\Rightarrow (2):$ By passing to the completion, we may assume that $R$ is complete (cf. \cite  [ Proposition 3.3]{Sch}).

We argue by induction on $t$. When $\ t=1$, there is nothing to prove, since Lemma \ref{2.2} and the assumptions imply that
$$\begin{array}{ll} \operatorname{Supp} (\mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M)) = \operatorname{Supp} (\mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M)) \cap V(\frak{a}) \subseteq V(\frak{m}).
\end{array}
$$
Hence $\ \mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M)\ $ is Artinian. To this end note that $  \mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M) $ is a finitely generated submodule of $M$. So suppose that $t> 1$ and the result has been proved for smaller values of $t$. Put $\overline {M} =M/H^0_{\frak{a}}(M)$. From the short exact sequences
$$\begin{array}{ll} 0 \longrightarrow H^{0}_{\frak{a}}(M ) \longrightarrow M \longrightarrow \overline{M} \longrightarrow 0
\end{array}
$$
and by \cite[Proposition 3.11]{Sch}), we get the following long exact sequence
$$\begin{array}{ll} ... \longrightarrow \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(H^{0}_{\frak{a}}(M )) \longrightarrow \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M) \longrightarrow \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(\overline{M}) \longrightarrow \mathfrak{F}^{i+1}_{\frak{a}}(H^{0}_{\frak{a}}(M ))\longrightarrow ....
\end{array}
$$
As $\mathfrak{F}^j_{\frak{a}}(H^{0}_{\frak{a}}(M ))= H^j_{\frak{m}}(H^0_{\frak{a}}(M))$ is an Artinian $R$-module for every $j \in \mathbb {Z}$ (\cite  [ Theorem 7.1.3]{Br-Sh}) then, one can see that $\ \operatorname{Supp} (\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(\overline {M})) \subseteq V(\frak{a})$ for all $i< t$. Hence, it is enough to show that $\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(\overline {M})$ is Artinian, so we may assume that $H^0_{\frak{a}}(M) = 0 $. Thus, there exists an $M$-regular element $x$ in ${\frak{a}}$ such that from the short exact sequence
$$\begin{array}{ll} 0 \longrightarrow M \stackrel{x}{\rightarrow}  M \longrightarrow  M/xM= \widetilde{M}\longrightarrow 0
\end{array}
$$
we deduce the next long exact sequence
$$\begin{array}{ll} ... \longrightarrow \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M ) \stackrel{x}{\rightarrow} \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M) \longrightarrow \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(\widetilde{M}) \longrightarrow \mathfrak{F}^{i+1}_{\frak{a}}(M)\longrightarrow ....\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ (\ast)
\end{array}
$$
Since   $\ \operatorname{Supp} (\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)) \subseteq V(\frak{a}) \ $ for all $i < t$, it follows from the above long exact sequence that $ \ \operatorname{Supp} (\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(\widetilde{M})) \subseteq V(\frak{a}) \ $ for all $\ i < {t-1} \ $. Hence, by induction hypothesis we have
$\ \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(\widetilde{M}) \ $ is Artinian for all  $\ i < {t-1}$. Therefore in the view of $(\ast)$,    $\ ( 0 :_{\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)}   x ) \ $ is  Artinian for all $\ i < t$ .

On the other hand since $\ \operatorname{Supp} (\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)) \subseteq V(\frak{a})\ $ for all $i< t \ $, one can see that
$$\begin{array}{ll} \ \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M) = \bigcup ( 0 :_{\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)}   {\frak{a}^\alpha} ) \subseteq \bigcup ( 0 :_{\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)} {x^\alpha}) \subseteq \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)
\end{array}$$
so $ \ \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M) = \bigcup ( 0 :_{\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)} {x^\alpha}) \ $. Therefore by \cite[Theorem 1.3]{Mel}, $\ \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)\ $ will be Artinian for all $i<t$.

 $(2)\Rightarrow (4):$ Since $\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)$ is $\frak{a}$-adically complete for every $i \in \mathbb {Z}\ $(cf. \cite[Theorem 3.9]{Sch} or  \cite[Remark 3.1]{H-St} ), we get $\bigcap_{n}\frak{a} ^n \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)=0$. Moreover for all $i <t$,  $\ \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)$ is Artinian. Hence,   there is an integer $u$ such that $\frak{a} ^u \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)=0$.

 $(4)\Rightarrow (3)$ is obvious.

$(1)\Rightarrow (5):$  By passing to the completion we may assume that $R$ is complete. We use induction on $t$. Let $t =1$. As $\operatorname{Supp} (\mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M)) \subseteq V(\frak{m}) $ so $\mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M)  $ must be zero. Otherwise since
$$\begin{array}{ll} \ \emptyset \neq \operatorname{Ass} ( \mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M) ) \subseteq \operatorname{Supp} ( \mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M) ) \subseteq V({\frak{m}})
\end{array}$$
then,
$$\begin{array}{ll} \ \frak{m} \in \operatorname{Ass} ( \mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(M) )= \{ \frak{p} \in \operatorname{Ass} M ;  \dim(R/\frak{a}+\frak{p}) = 0 \},
\end{array}$$
this is contradiction to $\operatorname{depth} M > 0$.

Now suppose that $ \operatorname{depth} M \geq t> 1$ and that  the result has been proved for smaller values of $t$. By this inductive assumption,   $\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)=0$ for $i=0,1,...,t-2$ and it only remains for us to prove that $\mathfrak{F}^{t-1}_{\frak{a}}(M)=0$.

Since $ \operatorname{depth} M > 1$  then, there exists $x \in {\frak{m}} \ $ that is an $M$-regular element. Consider the short exact sequence
$$\begin{array}{ll} \ 0 \rightarrow M \stackrel{x^l}{\rightarrow} M \rightarrow M/x^l M = \bar{M} \rightarrow 0
\end{array}$$
for every $l$.  Thus, we have the following long exact sequence
$$\begin{array}{ll} \ ... \rightarrow \mathfrak{F}^{i-1}_{\frak{a}}(\bar{M}) \rightarrow \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M) \stackrel{x^l}{\rightarrow} \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)\rightarrow \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(\bar{M}) \rightarrow ...
\end{array}$$
for every $l$.

As $\ \operatorname{depth} \bar{M}= \operatorname{depth} M -1> 0\ $  and for all $ i< t-1$,  $\ \operatorname{Supp} (\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(\bar{M})) \subseteq V(\frak{m})$ then, by inductive hypothesis $\ \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(\bar{M}) = 0 \ $  for all $\  i< t-1$ . Thus, for every $l$, $\ ( 0:_{\mathfrak{F}^{t-1}_{\frak{a}}(M)} x^l)$ is a homomorphic image of $\mathfrak{F}^{t-2}_{\frak{a}}(\bar{M})$. Hence, $\ ( 0:_{\mathfrak{F}^{t-1}_{\frak{a}}(M)} x^l) = 0 \ $ for every $l$.

Take into account that by assumption $\operatorname{Supp} (\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)) \subseteq V(\frak{m})$ for every $i<t$. Then,  $\ {\mathfrak{F}^{t-1}_{\frak{a}}(M)}  = \cup ( 0:_{\mathfrak{F}^{t-1}_{\frak{a}}(M)} x^l) = 0 \ $ . This completes the proof.
$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box

name: Theorem \ref1.1

title: Definition
body_md:
\label{3.1} (cf. \cite {R}) Let $R$ be a ring and $M$ an $R$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]  Let $S$ be a  multiplicative closed subset of $R$ and $D_{R}(-):= \operatorname{Hom}_{R}(-,E_{R})$, where $E_{R}$ is the injective hull of $\oplus R/\frak{m}$, the sum running over all maximal ideals $\frak{m}$ of $R$. The colocalization of $M$ relative to $S$ is the $S^{-1}R$-module $S_{-1}M=D_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}D_R(M))$. If $S=R \setminus \frak{p}\ $ for some prime ideal $\frak{p}\in \operatorname{Spec}(R)$, we write $^{\frak{p}}M$ for $S_{-1}M$.
\item[(2)]  The cosupport of $M$ is defined as follows
$$\begin{array}{ll} \ \operatorname{CoSupp}_R M := \{ \frak{p}\in \operatorname{Spec}(R):\ ^{\frak{p}}M \neq 0 \}.
\end{array}$$
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{3.2} (cf. \cite [Theorem 2.7]{R}) Let $R$ be a ring and $M$ an $R$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] $\operatorname{CoSupp} M =\operatorname{Supp} D_{R}(M)$.
\item[(2)] If $M$ is finitely generated, then $\operatorname{CoSupp} M = V(\operatorname{Ann} M)\cap \max(R)$.
\item[(3)] $\operatorname{CoSupp} M =\emptyset $ if and only if $M=0$.
\item[(4)]  $\operatorname{CoSupp} M \subseteq V(\operatorname{Ann} M)$.
\item[(5)] If $\ 0 \rightarrow M^{'} \rightarrow M \rightarrow M^{''} \rightarrow 0$ is exact, then $\operatorname{CoSupp} M = \operatorname{CoSupp} M^{'} \cup \operatorname{CoSupp} M^{''}$.
\item[(6)] If $M$ is representable, then $\operatorname{CoSupp} M = V(\operatorname{Ann} M)$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{3.3} Let $R$ be a ring and $M$ and $N$ be  $R$-modules. Then the following statements are true:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] $\operatorname{CoSupp} (M)$ is stable under specialization, i.e.
$$\begin{array}{ll} \  \frak{p} \in \operatorname{Cosupp} (M) , \frak{p} \subseteq \frak{q} \Rightarrow \frak{q} \in \operatorname{Cosupp} (M).
\end{array}$$
 \item[(2)] Let $M$ be a finite module, then  $\operatorname{CoSupp} (M \otimes_R N)\subseteq \operatorname{Supp} M \cap \operatorname{CoSupp} N$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
head: manual

title: Lemma
body_md: \label{3.4} Let $\frak{a}$ be an ideal of a ring $R$. Let $N$ be an Artinian $R$-module with $\operatorname{Att}_R (N)\subseteq V(\frak{a})$. Then $\operatorname{CoSupp} N \subseteq V(\frak{a})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $N$ is an Artinian module then, the following descending chain
$$\begin{array}{ll} \   \frak{a} N \supseteq \frak{a}^2 N \supseteq ... \supseteq \frak{a}^n N  \supseteq ...
\end{array}$$
of submodules of $N$ is stable, i.e. there exists an integer $k$ that $\frak{a}^k N= \frak{a}^{k+1} N$. As  $\operatorname{Att}_R (N/\frak{a}^k N)=\operatorname{Att}_R (N) \cap V(\frak{a})$ (cf. \cite[Proposition 5.2]{Mel-Sch}) and   $\operatorname{CoSupp} (N/\frak{a}^k N) \subseteq V(\frak{a})$ by virtue of Proposition \ref{3.3}, hence, by passing to $N/\frak{a}^k N$ we may assume that  $\frak{a}^k N=0$.

Let $\frak{p} \in \operatorname{CoSupp} N$ then, $^{\frak{p}}N \neq 0$. Thus, for every $s \in S= R \setminus \frak{p}$, $sN \neq 0$ (cf. \cite[2.1]{R}). On the other hand   $\bigcap_n \frak{a}^nN=\frak{a}^k N=0$, hence, for every $s \in S$, $sN \not \subseteq \frak{a}^tN$. It follows that for all $s \in S$, $s \notin \frak{a}^t$ and clearly  $\frak{p} \in V(\frak{a})$.
$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box
head: manual

title: Corollary
body_md: \label{3.5} Let $i \in \mathbb {Z}$. Let $(R,\frak{m})$ be a local ring and  $M$ be a finitely generated $R$-module. Assume that  $\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)$ is an Artinian $R$-module, then $\operatorname{CoSupp} \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M) \subseteq V(\frak{a})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As $\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)$ is Artinian and $\frak{a}$-adically complete so, there exists an integer $k$ such that $\bigcap_{n \geq 1} \frak{a}^n \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)= \frak{a}^k \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)=0$. Hence, \cite[Proposition 7.2.11]{Br-Sh} implies that $\operatorname{Att} \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M)\subseteq V(\frak{a})$ and in the light of Lemma \ref{3.4} $\ \operatorname{CoSupp} \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(M) \subseteq V(\frak{a})$.
$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box
head: manual

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{3.6} Converse of Corollary \ref{3.5} is not true in general.  Let $R=k[\left| x \right|]$ denote the formal power series ring over a field $k$. Put $\frak{a}=(x)R$.  Then
$$\begin{array}{ll} \  \operatorname{CoSupp} \mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(R) =\operatorname{Supp} D_R(D_R (H^{1}_{\frak{a}}(R)))= \operatorname{Supp} H^{1}_{\frak{a}}(R)\subseteq V(\frak{a})
\end{array}$$
but $\mathfrak{F}^0_{\frak{a}}(R)$ is not Artinian .
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{3.7} Let $(R, \frak{m})$ be a $d$-dimensional  local ring. Let $M$ be a finitely generated $R$-module. Then
$$\begin{array}{ll} \  \mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( M)\cong \mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( R)\otimes_{R}M,
\end{array}$$
where $c:= \dim R/\frak{a}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
At first note that by definition of inverse limit, $\mathfrak{F}^j_{\frak{a}}(-)$ preserves finite direct sum, for every $j \in \mathbb {Z}$. Furthermore  $\mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}(-)$ is a right exact functor (cf. \cite[Theorem 4.5]{Sch}).
Hence, by Watts' Theorem ( \cite[Theorem 3.33]{Ro})  the claim is  proved. $\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box
head: manual

title: Proof
body_md:
(1): Since $\mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( M) \cong \mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a} (R/J)}( M)$,  by Independence Theorem \cite [4.2.1]{Br-Sh}, we may replace $R$ by $R/J$ to assume that $M$ is faithful. Note that for $\dim R/(\frak{a}, J) < c$, there is nothing to prove because, $\mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( M)= 0$.

In the view of lemma \ref{3.7} and \cite[Proposition 2.5]{R}, for every $\frak{p} \in \operatorname{Spec} R$
$$\begin{array}{ll} \    ^{\frak{p}}\mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( M) \cong M_{\frak{p}} \otimes_{R_{\frak{p}}}\  ^{\frak{p}}\mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( R).
\end{array}$$


As  $M_{\frak{p}}$ is a faithful $R_{\frak{p}}$-module, \cite[Corollary 4.3]{V} implies that $M_{\frak{p}} \otimes_{R}\  ^{\frak{p}}\mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( R)=0$ if and only if
 $ ^{\frak{p}}\mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( R)=0$, which completes the proof.

(2): To prove,  we use the localization instead of colocalization in the proof of $(1)$.
$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box
head: manual
name: Theorem \ref1.2

title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] Let $\frak{p} \in \operatorname{Coass} (M)$, then, it implies that $0\neq \operatorname{Hom}_{R_{\frak{p}}}(R_{\frak{p}}/\frak{p} R_{\frak{p}},D_{R}(M)_{\frak{p}})$. Note that  it remains nonzero by taking $\operatorname{Hom}_{R_{\frak{p}}}(-,E_{R_{\frak{p}}}(R_{\frak{p}}/\frak{p} R_{\frak{p}}))$ and consequently $\frak{p} \in \operatorname{CoSupp} (M)$.

\item[(2)]   Let $\frak{p} \in \min \operatorname{CoSupp} (M)=  \min \operatorname{Supp} D_{R}(M)$, so, $\frak{p} \in \min \operatorname{Ass} D_{R}(M)$. It follows that $\frak{p} \in \min \operatorname{Coass} (M)$.

\item[(3)] It is clear by (1) and (2).$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box
head: manual

title: Lemma
body_md: \label{4.2} Let $(R, \frak{m})$ be a local ring and $M$ be an $R$-module. The set of  minimal primes in $\operatorname{CoSupp}(M)$ is finite if and only if $\operatorname{CoSupp}(M)$ is a closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec} R$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\operatorname{CoSupp} (M)= V(\frak{b})$ for some ideal $\frak{b}$ of $R$. As $R$ is Noetherian then so is $R/\frak{b}$. It turns out that the set of minimal elements of $\operatorname{CoSupp}(M)$ is finite.

For the reverse direction, let $\frak{p}_{1},..., \frak{p}_{t}$ be the minimal prime ideals of $\operatorname{CoSupp} (M)$. Put $\frak{q}:= \cap_{i} \frak{p}_{i}$. We claim that $\operatorname{CoSupp}  M= V(\frak{q})$.

It is clear that $\operatorname{CoSupp} (M)\subseteq V(\frak{q})$. For the opposite direction assume that there is a prime ideal $Q \supset \frak{q}$. Then $Q \supset \frak{p}_{j}$, for some $1 \leq j \leq t$ so the proof follows by \ref{3.3}(1). $\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box
head: manual

title: Theorem
body_md: \label{4.3} Let $\frak{a}$ be an ideal of a local ring $(R,\frak{m})$ and $M$ a finitely generated R-module. Assume that $\dim M/\frak{a} M > 0$. Then $\mathfrak{F}^{\dim M/\frak{a} M}_{\frak{a}}( M)$ is not a finitely generated $R$-module.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $c:= \dim M/\frak{a} M$. In the contrary assume that $\mathfrak{F}^{c}_{\frak{a}}( M)$ is a finitely generated $R$-module. Let $x \in \frak{m}$ be a parameter element of $M/\frak{a} M$. Hence, \cite[Theorem 3.15]{Sch} implies the following long exact sequence
$$\begin{array}{ll} \  ... \rightarrow \operatorname{Hom} (R_x, \mathfrak{F}^{c}_{\frak{a}}( M)) \rightarrow \mathfrak{F}^{c}_{\frak{a}}( M) \rightarrow \mathfrak{F}^{c}_{(\frak{a},x)}( M) \rightarrow ...,
\end{array}$$
where $i \in \mathbb {Z}$.
As $\dim M/(\frak{a},x) M < \dim M/\frak{a} M\ $ then, $\mathfrak{F}^{c}_{(\frak{a},x)}( M)=0$. Now let $f \in \operatorname{Hom} (R_x, \mathfrak{F}^{c}_{\frak{a}}( M))$. Fix an arbitrary integer $n$, so
$$\begin{array}{ll} \  f(1/x^n)=x^m f(1/x^{m+n}) \in x^m \mathfrak{F}^{c}_{\frak{a}}( M),
\end{array}$$
for every integer $m$. It implies that $f(1/x^n) \in \bigcap_{m} x^m \mathfrak{F}^{c}_{\frak{a}}( M)=0$ by Krull's Theorem and hence, $f=0$. Now it follows that $\mathfrak{F}^{c}_{\frak{a}}( M)=0$, which is a contradiction, see \cite[Theorem 4.5]{Sch}.
$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box
head: manual

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{4.4} Let $\frak{a}$ be an ideal of a  complete Gorenstein local  ring $(R, \frak{m})$ and $c:= \dim R/\frak{a}$. Let $M$  be a  finitely generated  $R$-module. Then
$$\begin{array}{ll} \   \operatorname{Coass}_R (\mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( M)) = \operatorname{Supp}_R (M)  \cap \operatorname{Ass} (H^{\operatorname{ht} \frak{a}}_{\frak{a}}(R)).
\end{array}$$
In particular,  $\ \operatorname{Coass}_R (\mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( M))$ is finite.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
$$\begin{array}{ll} \   \operatorname{Coass}_R (\mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( M))& = \operatorname{Coass}_R (\mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( R)\otimes_R M)
\\& = \operatorname{Supp}_R M \cap  \operatorname{Coass}_R (\mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( R))
\\& = \operatorname{Supp}_R M \cap \operatorname{Ass}_R (H^{\operatorname{ht} \frak{a}}_{\frak{a}}(R))
\end{array}$$
where the first equality is clear by Lemma \ref{3.7}, the second equality follows by \cite[Theorem 1.21]{Y}.
$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box
head: manual

title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{4.5} Keep the notations and hypotheses in Proposition \ref{4.4},
$$\begin{array}{ll} \     \mathfrak{F}^c_{\frak{a}}( M)= 0 \Longleftrightarrow  \operatorname{Supp}_R (M)  \cap \operatorname{Ass} (H^{\operatorname{ht} \frak{a}}_{\frak{a}}(R)) =\emptyset.
\end{array}$$
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: \label{4.6} Let $i \in \mathbb {Z}$. Let $\frak{a} \subset R$ be an ideal of a ring $R$. If $\operatorname{Coass}_R \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}( R)$ is finite, then so is  $\operatorname{Coass}_R \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}( R/H^0_{\frak{a}}(R))$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the exact sequence
$$\begin{array}{ll} \    0 \rightarrow H^0_{\frak{a}}(R) \rightarrow R \rightarrow  R/H^0_{\frak{a}}(R)=\overline{R} \rightarrow 0.
\end{array}$$
It provides the following long exact sequence
$$\begin{array}{ll} \    ... \rightarrow \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(H^0_{\frak{a}}(R)) {\stackrel{\psi}{\rightarrow}} \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(R) \stackrel{\varphi}{\rightarrow} \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(\overline{R}) \rightarrow \mathfrak{F}^{i+1}_{\frak{a}}(H^0_{\frak{a}}(R)) \rightarrow ..., \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ (\ast)
\end{array}$$
for every $i$.

As $\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(H^0_{\frak{a}}(R))=H^i_{\frak{m}}(H^0_{\frak{a}}(R))$ is Artinian, it follows that $\operatorname{Coass} (\mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(H^0_{\frak{a}}(R)))$ is finite.

By virtue of $(\ast)$, we get the following short exact sequence
$$\begin{array}{ll} \    0 \rightarrow  U \rightarrow  \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}(\overline{R}) \rightarrow U^{'} \rightarrow 0,
\end{array}$$
where $U=\operatorname{coker} \psi$ and $U^{'}=\operatorname{coker} \varphi$. It implies that $\operatorname{Coass} \mathfrak{F}^i_{\frak{a}}( \overline{R})$ is finite. To this end note that $\operatorname{Coass} (U)$ is finite by \cite[Theorem 1.10]{Y} and $\operatorname{Coass} (U^{'})$ is finite as $\mathfrak{F}^{i+1}_{\frak{a}}(H^0_{\frak{a}}(R))$
is Artinian.
$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box

title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] Let $\frak{p} \in \operatorname{Coass} \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R)$.  As $ \mathfrak{F}^{d}_{\frak{a}}(R)=0$ then, by \cite[Theorem 4.5]{Sch} we have
$$\begin{array}{ll} \  \dim R/(\frak{a},\frak{p}) \leq \dim R/\frak{a} \leq d-1.
\end{array}$$
On the other hand $\frak{p} \in \operatorname{Coass} (R/\frak{p} \otimes_R \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R))$, because
$$\begin{array}{ll} \  \operatorname{Coass} (R/\frak{p} \otimes_R \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R))= \operatorname{Supp} R/\frak{p} \cap \operatorname{Coass} \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R).
\end{array}$$
 It yields with the similar argument to lemma \ref{3.7} that $0 \neq R/\frak{p} \otimes_R \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R)=\mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R/\frak{p})$. So, we have $ \dim R/(\frak{a},\frak{p})\geq d-1$. It completes the proof.

\item[(2)] Let $ \frak{p} \in \operatorname{Assh}(R) \cap \operatorname{Coass} \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R)$. Then, similar to $(1)$,  $\mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R/\frak{p})\neq 0$ and  moreover $\operatorname{Rad} (\frak{a}+ \frak{p}) \neq \frak{m}$. To this end note that if $\operatorname{Rad} (\frak{a}+ \frak{p}) = \frak{m}$ then,  $ \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R/\frak{p})=0 $ by Grothendieck's vanishing Theorem.

\item[(3)] Let $\frak{p} \in \operatorname{Spec} R$ and  $\dim (R/(\frak{a},\frak{p}))= d-1 $. Then, it follows that $\emptyset \neq \operatorname{Coass} \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R/\frak{p}) = \operatorname{Supp}(R/\frak{p}) \cap \operatorname{Coass}\mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R)$.
Let $\frak{q} \in \operatorname{Coass}\mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R)$ then, $\frak{q} \supseteq \frak{p}$, but by assumption $\frak{q}$ is minimal so we deduce that $\frak{q}=\frak{p}$.
$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{4.8}
 The inclusion in Theorem \ref{4.7}(2) is not an equality in general. For example Let $R=k[[x,y,z]]$ denote the formal power series ring in three  variables over a field $k$. Let  $\frak{a}=(x,y)$ be an ideal of $R$ which is of  dimension one and put $\frak{p}=0$. It is clear that  $\mathfrak{F}^{3-1}_{\frak{a}}(R)=0=\mathfrak{F}^{3}_{\frak{a}}(R)$, that is $\operatorname{Coass} \mathfrak{F}^{3-1}_{\frak{a}}(R)= \emptyset$.

title: Lemma
body_md: \label{4.9} Let $(R,\frak{m})$ be a complete local ring and $\frak{a}$ an ideal of $R$. Let $\frak{p}$ be a minimal prime ideal of $\frak{a}$. Then   $\frak{q} \in \operatorname{Coass}_R(\widehat{R_{\frak{p}}})$ implies that $\frak{q} \subseteq \frak{p}$, where the functor $\ \widehat{.}\ $ denotes the completion functor.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is straightforward. Let $\frak{q} \in \operatorname{Coass}_R(\widehat{R_{\frak{p}}})$, then
$$\begin{array}{ll} \   0 \neq  \operatorname{Hom}_R (R/\frak{q} , \operatorname{Hom}_R( \widehat{R_{\frak{p}}}, E_R(R/\frak{m}))) = \operatorname{Hom}_R (R/\frak{q} \otimes_R \widehat{R_{\frak{p}}}, E_R(R/\frak{m})).
\end{array}$$
It yields that
$$\begin{array}{ll} \   0 \neq  R/\frak{q} \otimes_R \widehat{R_{\frak{p}}} = R/\frak{q} \otimes_R R_{\frak{p}} \otimes_{R_{\frak{p}}} \widehat{R_{\frak{p}}}.
\end{array}$$
It is clear that $R_{\frak{p}}/\frak{q} R_{\frak{p}} \neq 0$ and so $\frak{q}$ must be contained in $\frak{p}$.
$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box
head: manual

title: Proof
body_md:
For $d>2$ and $d=1$, the claim is clear.

 Let $d=2$. Suppose that $\frak{p}_1,..., \frak{p}_r$ are the minimal prime ideals of $\frak{a}$. Put $S= \bigcap^r_{i=1}(R \setminus \frak{p}_i)$ and choose $y \in \frak{m} \setminus \bigcup^r_{i=1} \frak{p}_i$. By  \cite[Theorem 2.2.4]{Br-Sh}, for any $n \in \mathbb {N}$ we have
 $$\begin{array}{ll} \ 0 \rightarrow H^0_{\frak{m}}(R/\frak{a}^n) \rightarrow R/\frak{a}^n \rightarrow D_{(y)}(R/\frak{a}^n) \rightarrow H^1_{\frak{m}}(R/\frak{a}^n) \rightarrow 0,
\end{array}$$
where $D_{(y)}(R/\frak{a}^n)$ is the $(y)$-transform functor. One can see that $D_{(y)}(R/\frak{a}^n)\cong R_S/\frak{a}^n R_S$, so we get the following exact sequence
 $$\begin{array}{ll} \ 0 \rightarrow H^0_{\frak{m}}(R/\frak{a}^n) \rightarrow R/\frak{a}^n \rightarrow R_S/\frak{a}^n R_S \rightarrow H^1_{\frak{m}}(R/\frak{a}^n) \rightarrow 0.
\end{array}$$
Furthermore $R_S/\frak{a}^n R_S \cong \oplus^r_{i=1} R_{\frak{p}_i}/ \frak{a}^n R_{\frak{p}_i}$.
All the modules in the above exact sequence satisfy the Mittag-Leffler condition so by applying inverse limits we get
$$\begin{array}{ll} \ 0  \rightarrow R/\mathfrak{F}^{0}_{\frak{a}}(R) \rightarrow \oplus^r_{i=1} \widehat{R_{\frak{p}_i}} \rightarrow \mathfrak{F}^{1}_{\frak{a}}(R) \rightarrow 0.
\end{array}$$
It yields that $\operatorname{Coass}_R (\mathfrak{F}^{1}_{\frak{a}}(R)) \subseteq \bigcup^r_{i=1} \operatorname{Coass}_R(\widehat{R_{\frak{p}_i}}) \subseteq \operatorname{Coass}_R (\mathfrak{F}^{1}_{\frak{a}}(R)) \cup \{ \frak{m}\}$. In the view of lemma \ref{4.9}, $\operatorname{Coass}_R (\mathfrak{F}^{1}_{\frak{a}}(R)) = \bigcup^r_{i=1} \operatorname{Coass}_R(\widehat{R_{\frak{p}_i}})$. Now the claim is proved by \cite[Beispiel 2.4]{Z}. To this end note that $\operatorname{Coass}_R(\widehat{R_{\frak{p}_i}})=\operatorname{Coass}_{R_{\frak{p}_i}}(\widehat{R_{\frak{p}_i}}) \cap R$ for every $i \in \{ 1,...,r \}$.
$\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \Box

name: Theorem \ref1.4

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{4.10} Keep the notations and hypotheses in Theorem \ref{1.4}  and let $M$ be a finitely generated $R$-module. As $R$ is complete so by Cohen's structure Theorem, there exists a Gorenstein local ring $(S,\frak{n})$ where $R$ is a homomorphic image of  $S$ and $\dim R= \dim S$. Then by virtue of \ref{3.7} we have
 $$\begin{array}{ll} \ \operatorname{Ass}_R H^1_{\frak{a} S}(M,S) \subseteq \operatorname{Coass} \mathfrak{F}^{d-1}_{\frak{a}}(R)
\end{array}$$
is finite.
